proposed_widenings.name: ModifyRollAdvantageOperation (OngoingOperation variant)
proposed_widenings.justification: Blur's core mechanic is disadvantage on attack rolls made against the caster. The current OngoingOperation union only has roll_modifier (numeric DiceDelta via modify_roll_numeric) and damage_on_hit. No variant exists for advantage/disadvantage state modification on an ongoing basis. The v4 atom modify_roll_advantage exists but is unreachable from the ongoing_effect family.
proposed_widenings.evidence: any creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you

proposed_widenings.name: rolls_targeting_attachment direction on OngoingOperation
proposed_widenings.justification: Blur modifies incoming attack rolls (those targeting the attachment subject). The existing roll_modifier in Bless modifies outgoing rolls made by the attachment targets. A new advantage-state operation variant would need to specify direction: 'rolls targeting the attachment' vs 'rolls made by the attachment'. This may be expressible as a field on the new variant rather than a separate variant.
proposed_widenings.evidence: any creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you

proposed_widenings.name: PerceptualSenseFilter on OngoingOperation
proposed_widenings.justification: Blur has an immunity clause: attackers with Blindsight or Truesight are immune to the disadvantage. No surface encoding exists for sense-based bypass filters on ongoing operations.
proposed_widenings.evidence: An attacker is immune to this effect if it perceives you with Blindsight or Truesight.

notes: The ongoing_effect family and self attachment are both correct. The sole blocker is the missing OngoingOperation variant for advantage/disadvantage modification. All atoms needed (modify_roll_advantage, concentrate, expire, action_quota, spell_slot) are in v4. The immunity clause (Blindsight/Truesight bypass) is a secondary gap with no current surface analog — could be deferred or encoded as a filter field on the new operation variant.
